thread:
Alex W: Heads-up — want to lock the benchmark narrative for the launch deck. thinking we should pivot from 'average latency' to a fat-tail story that shows predictable cost vs worst-case SLA risk. thoughts? :thinking_face:
Maria G: love that. median is meaningless for customer infra. CDF or P99/P99.9 comparison is much clearer for product teams. :chart_with_upwards_trend:
Ryan D: Agreed. Also include a small panel for token cost delta (quantized vs fp16) — folks always ask about dollars. maybe a 2x2: latency tail on left, $/1k tokens on right.
Sophie L: For marketing copy we can do "Same accuracy, better unit economics at tail" — but avoid heavy engineering jargon. call out "predictable tail latency" + a concrete example: 95% of requests < 120ms, 99.9% < 520ms.
Alex W: Nice. Can you rough those numbers from the latest bench CSV? Ryan, do we have p50/p95/p99/p999 for the production slice (chat+streaming)?
Ryan D: yes. quick raw snippet below (prod slice, mixed customer traffic):
```
model, p50_ms, p95_ms, p99_ms, p999_ms, cost_per_1k_tokens_usd
redwood-llama-13b-q4, 60, 180, 320, 620, 0.45
redwood-vicuna-13b, 80, 220, 460, 1100, 0.72
redwood-ggml-quant8, 90, 260, 480, 900, 0.33
```
Sophie L: This is gold. For visuals: left chart = CDF lines for the three models (x=latency ms, y=% requests). right chart = stacked bar of cost components (compute vs infra) or a simple $/1k tokens bar so it's easy to scan.
Maria G: Also want an inset that shows routing strategy: "fastpath for interactive customers, slowpath with cheaper models for batch/embeddings". That sets up the Dedicated/Private differentiation.
Alex W: Good call. For the launch post copy, keep it simple: 3 bullets — 1) latency tail matters, 2) cost tradeoffs are model+config choices, 3) Redwood gives predictable SLOs + fallbacks. Can you draft?
Sophie L: Draft in thread: "Most metrics hide the tails. Our benchmarks show 99.9th percentile can be 5x the median — and that has real $ impact. Redwood's routing, quantization profiles, and batching shrink that tail while lowering unit costs."
Maria G: Love. Add CTA: "Sign up for the webinar: benchmark deep-dive + live Q&A" with a single slide link. MarketingBot: webinar-registrations link -> https://redwood.ai/webinar-benchmarks (auto-posted) :calendar:
Ryan D: Ops ask: we should pin the exact bench commit SHA and dataset slice in the notes so engineering can reproduce charts. I'll attach after this thread.
Alex W: Action items: Sophie to draft post + slide copy by EOD tomorrow; Maria to wire the webinar CTA and routing; Ryan to attach bench CSV + SHA. I'll review and compress into 3 visuals. If anyone disagrees with the emphasis on tails, say now. :+1:
Sophie L: on it. will aim for punchy copy and a simplified two-chart visual.
Maria G: I'll set up the registration page and add the routing CTA to the launch email sequence.
Ryan D: attaching SHA in follow-up (will post in this thread).
